=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit

# Project Kestrel: Buyer review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall view:** The package is not "fair and balanced". It is seller-favourable on liability, with limits applied to every claim type, no fraud carve-out, a data-room-wide disclosure and a knowledge bar. Several items that should be conditions, price adjustments or specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, the privacy incident) are recast as ordinary warranty or post-Completion matters. The Disclosure Letter itself concedes the open facts, which helps us. Those concessions are the basis for treating these items outside the warranty regime.

I have only the documents above. Benchmarks are my judgment, not fixed market rules, and some figures need confirming against the full SPA and DD record.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A cap of 30-40% for general warranties, with uncapped or separate caps for other categories (see N-004, N-011, N-012, N-016).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 40% and accept no less than about 30%. The identified exposures (Bluefen about AUD 3.6m revenue, Riverlark about AUD 3.2m) leave little headroom under AUD 4.8m. The cap should apply only to general warranties.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis of AUD 10k or less, with related claims aggregated. A tipping basket (first-dollar recovery) of about 0.5% (about AUD 120k).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure and counter with a tipping basket. A deductible plus a high de minimis erodes recovery on many small, real issues.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so that at least two audit cycles are covered.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months for general warranties only. Eighteen months may expire before a full audit cycle surfaces problems, and the "applies to all Claims" language undermines the longer periods needed elsewhere.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate fundamental regime. The cap should be 100% of the price, with no de minimis or basket and a long claim period (6 years, or longer if the SPA is a deed). Include capacity, authority, title, no encumbrances, and share capital.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title failure goes to the root of what we are buying, and a AUD 4.8m cap against a AUD 24m price is unacceptable for it.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None offered. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause applies to fraud, dishonest concealment or wilful misconduct, including by the Seller's representatives. Statutory rights that cannot lawfully be excluded must also be preserved.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on it. A seller cannot credibly resist excluding its own fraud from the caps.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1-1.2, Sch 7).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. A data-room-wide disclosure should not qualify warranties. Disclosure must not qualify specific indemnities, fundamental warranties, tax or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. It would let the Seller disclose away the warranties covering the very issues in this letter. DL 1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable only if it does not narrow our rights.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Delete cl 8.3, and add a pro-sandbagging clause confirming that knowledge does not prejudice any claim. At most, accept actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, and never against indemnities, fundamental warranties or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Combined with N-006, it removes almost all warranty protection, and it would defeat the specific indemnities we need for the issues we already know about.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours", with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL para 2 admits there is no consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m).
- **Buyer should want:** A condition precedent requiring Bluefen's written, unconditional consent under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with any cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by the Buyer alone. Add a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a Buyer-controlled condition. Losing a 30% customer would materially impair value, so "any consent" or "reasonable endeavours" is not enough.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion". About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and DL para 3 confirms it is not repaid and no discharge is provided.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment at Completion, as required by the debt-free/cash-free basis. This means a payout letter, direct payment to Riverlark out of the price in the funds flow, and security discharges (including PPSR) and releases delivered in escrow or at Completion. Riverlark's change-control position under cl 8.1 should be dealt with as well.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. It contradicts the debt-free/cash-free deal and leaves our asset encumbered.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k of DD-005 closing bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not in the funds flow. DL para 5 confirms that the amounts are absent from the funds flow and that on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer should want:** Treat the bonuses as Seller transaction costs or debt-like items, deducted from the price or paid through payroll from Seller funds at Completion. Include the employer on-costs (superannuation and NSW payroll tax, where applicable), which could add up to roughly AUD 70k and need confirming with tax advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Require deduction from the price, with an on-cost true-up, so the Buyer does not pay for them twice.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of the AUD 180k and proof of cleared payment before Completion, as a condition. Also a confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials under DD-004 cl 7.3. In addition, a specific indemnity for any loss from defects in IP ownership or claims by Ironquay, outside the basket and cap, and not qualified by disclosure. DL para 4 admits there is no receipt or assignment, and the AUD 180k open balance is not independently verified.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Fix the problem before Completion and keep a wider indemnity, because losing ownership of the SOW3 materials would affect the core product.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** The DD-006 matter is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Pre-Completion:** A covenant to complete the investigation and a notifiable-data-breach assessment under the Privacy Act, and to notify the OAIC and individuals if required. The statutory assessment period is 30 days from suspicion, so timing needs checking. The Buyer should have access to the findings and a say in the notices.
  - **Specific indemnity:** For investigation, notification, regulatory, third-party and remediation costs, uncapped or capped at a high level, and not qualified by disclosure. Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "not material". About 1,240 records are involved, access and scope are unknown, and DL para 6 itself disclaims any conclusion or loss figure. Use an indemnity and retention, not a warranty.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer should want:** Confirmation of whether each renewal is committed, terminable or already accrued or prepaid, and whether any was structured to sit beneath an approval or authority threshold. If committed beyond the ordinary course, treat as debt-like or adjust the price. Add an interim covenant requiring Buyer consent for renewals before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Don't accept the characterisation. DL para 8 declines to say they are ordinary-course or unavoidable, so verify before agreeing.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise, and cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to all Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. Caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance should apply to general warranty claims only.
- **Recommendation:** Reverse the default. Limits should apply only where expressly stated, otherwise the Seller's blanket language undoes every other protection we negotiate.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL para 10 says this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification before signing: ASIC and PPSR searches, the constitution and any pre-emption or transfer restrictions, issue and transfer history, and confirmation that no security or third-party rights exist over the shares (including under the Riverlark facility). Completion deliverables should include signed transfers and any discharges. The fundamental warranties in N-004 should then apply.
- **Recommendation:** Do our own verification. A register prepared by the Seller is not proof of good title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A separate pre-Completion tax indemnity or tax deed, with no basket or de minimis. The claim period should run to the amendment period (generally 4 years for most taxpayers, longer for fraud or evasion), with agreed conduct of claims. It should include on-costs on the bonuses and the NSW payroll tax treatment.
  - **IP:** Warranties covering ownership, employee and contractor assignments, no infringement, and open-source use. The title-type IP warranties should sit in the higher regime, with a link to the Ironquay indemnity (N-011).
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Nothing in the Seller Update addresses tax indemnities or IP ownership, so these terms are open.

---

### Suggested priorities
1. **Walk-away items:** N-005 (fraud), N-004 and N-015 (title), N-009 (Riverlark), N-008 (Bluefen).
2. **Value protection:** N-010 (bonuses), N-011 (Ironquay), N-012 (privacy), N-013 (Sandbar).
3. **Structure and numbers:** N-001 to N-003, N-006, N-007, N-014, N-016.

I can turn this into a mark-up issues list or draft replacement clauses for the SPA and Disclosure Letter if that would help.
